title: Sync Catalogs Response
description: Response from catalog sync or item availability operation. Exactly one of three shapes: (1) synchronous success — per-catalog results, availability update acknowledgements, and/or current-state query results; (2) terminal failure — errors array with no resources processed; (3) submitted task envelope — status 'submitted' with task_id when a catalog-only operation is queued. The submitted branch MAY carry advisory errors for non-blocking warnings; terminal failures belong in the error branch. These three shapes are mutually exclusive — a response has exactly one.

oneOf.title: SyncCatalogsSuccess
oneOf.description: Success response - sync operation processed catalogs (may include per-catalog failures)

dry_run.description: Whether this was a dry run (no actual changes made)

catalogs.description: Results for each catalog processed. Items with action='failed' indicate per-catalog validation/processing failures, not operation-level failures.

catalog_generation.description: Opaque token for this catalog incarnation. Sellers declaring catalog_item_availability_updates MUST return it for every accessible buyer-managed catalog result, including discovery. It remains stable across ordinary upserts and feed refreshes, changes after deletion and recreation, and is never reused for the same resolved account and catalog_id.

platform_id.description: Platform-specific ID assigned to the catalog

item_count.description: Total number of items in the catalog after sync. Required when action is 'created', 'updated', or 'unchanged'. Omitted on 'failed' and 'deleted'.

items_approved.description: Number of items approved by the platform. Populated when the platform performs item-level review.

items_pending.description: Number of items pending platform review. Common for product catalogs where items must pass content policy checks.

items_rejected.description: Number of items rejected by the platform. Check item_issues for rejection reasons.

item_issues.description: Per-item review outcomes. Ordinarily contains issues such as rejections and warnings. When media_buy.features.catalog_ingestion.item_status_reporting is per_item, terminal results for created, updated, or unchanged catalogs MUST include exactly one entry for every item in the resulting catalog, including approved and pending items, keyed by canonical item_id. This includes discovery-only reads of accessible buyer-managed catalogs: current statuses are returned without re-ingestion or restarting review. The number of unique item_id entries MUST equal item_count. Buyers MUST reject incomplete reports or duplicate item IDs. Replayed results are historical snapshots; a fresh idempotency_key obtains a current read. Dry-run outcomes are previews and do not prove live eligibility. Aggregate counts or a sparse issues list do not satisfy per_item reporting.

item_id.description: Canonical catalog item key, including approved and pending items when complete per-item reporting is declared.

last_synced_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the most recent sync was accepted by the platform

next_fetch_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the platform will next fetch the feed URL. Only present for URL-based catalogs with update_frequency.

changes.description: Field names that were modified (only present when action='updated')

errors.description: Validation or processing errors (only present when action='failed')

item_availability_updates.description: Acknowledgements for item_availability_updates. The array length MUST equal the request array length; entry N MUST have request_index N, occupy position N, and exactly echo catalog_id, catalog_generation, item_id, and action from request entry N. Buyers MUST reject the response as non-conformant if count, ordering, request_index, or echoed identity differs. Lenient-mode failures stay in their request positions. In strict mode, any per-entry failure instead produces the operation-level error branch before mutation and this array is absent.

item_availability_states.description: Current-state results for item_availability_queries, evaluated after updates in a mixed request. The array length MUST equal the request query length; entry N MUST have request_index N, occupy position N, and exactly echo catalog_id, catalog_generation, and item_id. Buyers MUST reject any mismatch. A replayed response is historical; use a fresh query idempotency_key before treating it as current after time-dependent expiry or catalog deletion/recreation.

sandbox.description: When true, this response contains simulated data from sandbox mode.
